---
title: "Utility Functions"
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(PKNCA)
library(dplyr)
conflicted::conflicts_prefer(dplyr::filter, dplyr::select, .quiet = TRUE)
```

## Overview

PKNCA exports several lower-level utility functions useful for data preparation, interval validation, and direct computation outside the full `PKNCAdata` → `pk.nca()` pipeline.

---

## BLQ concentration handling: `clean.conc.blq()`

Applies the BLQ-handling rule to a concentration vector **before** calculation. The full analysis pipeline applies this automatically, but `clean.conc.blq()` is useful for pre-processing or testing your own rule.

```{r}
conc <- c(0.5, 0.3, 0,    0.1, 0,    0.0, 0.02)
time <- c(0,   1,   2,    3,   4,    5,   6   )

# Drop BLQ (0) values
clean.conc.blq(conc, time, conc.blq = "drop")
```

```{r}
# Replace BLQ with half the LLOQ (= 0.05 here)
clean.conc.blq(conc, time, conc.blq = 0.05)
```

The `conc.blq` argument accepts:

- `"drop"` — remove BLQ rows
- `"keep"` — keep BLQ rows as-is
- A number — substitute BLQ values with that number

---

## NA concentration handling: `clean.conc.na()`

Removes or replaces NA concentrations. Internally called before AUC computation.

```{r}
conc_na <- c(0.5, NA, 0.3, 0.1, NA)
time_na <- c(0,   1,   2,   3,   4)

# Default: drop NAs
clean.conc.na(conc_na, time_na, conc.na = "drop")
```

```{r}
# Replace NAs with 0
clean.conc.na(conc_na, time_na, conc.na = 0)
```

---

## Concentration interpolation / extrapolation: `interp.extrap.conc()`

Interpolates or extrapolates a concentration at a target time given a known concentration-time profile. The `aucint.*` parameters use it internally when an interval boundary falls between two observed timepoints and no dosing data are given; with dosing data they use the dose-aware `interp.extrap.conc.dose()` instead.

```{r}
conc_ex <- c(10, 8, 5, 2.5, 1)
time_ex <- c(0,  1, 2, 4,   8)

# Interpolate at t = 3 (between t=2 and t=4)
interp.extrap.conc(conc = conc_ex, time = time_ex, time.out = 3)
```

```{r}
# Extrapolate beyond the last sample (t = 12):
# estimate lambda.z first, then pass it to interp.extrap.conc()
hl_ex <- pk.calc.half.life(conc = conc_ex, time = time_ex)
hl_ex$lambda.z

interp.extrap.conc(conc = conc_ex, time = time_ex, time.out = 12,
                   lambda.z = hl_ex$lambda.z)
```

The method (linear vs log-linear) follows the `auc.method` setting. Extrapolation beyond Tlast requires supplying `lambda.z` (the terminal slope) — the function never estimates λz itself, and without `lambda.z` the result is `NA`. The example above estimates it with `pk.calc.half.life()`, covered next. For interpolation around dose events, see the [Dose-Aware Interpolation chapter](dose-aware-interpolation.qmd) and the vignette [Methods for Dose-Aware Interpolation and Extrapolation](https://humanpred.github.io/pknca/articles/v21-methods-for-dose-aware-interpolation-and-extrapolation.html).

## Direct half-life computation: `pk.calc.half.life()`

Runs the full curve-stripping algorithm on raw concentration-time data and returns the selected half-life, λz, and associated diagnostics. Useful for batch processing outside the standard pipeline.

```{r}
subj1 <- as.data.frame(Theoph) |> filter(Subject == "1")

hl_result <- pk.calc.half.life(
  conc    = subj1$conc,
  time    = subj1$Time,
  options = PKNCA.options()
)

hl_result[c("half.life", "lambda.z", "r.squared", "lambda.z.n.points",
            "lambda.z.time.first", "span.ratio")]
```

This is the same function called internally by `pk.nca()` when `half.life = TRUE`.

---

## Direct AUC computation: `pk.calc.auc.all()`

Computes AUC directly on a concentration-time vector with the chosen integration method. It returns the AUC with a `"method"` attribute (≥ 0.13.0) naming that method — the text that `pk.nca()` moves into the `PPANMETH` column of its results.

```{r}
pk.calc.auc.all(
  conc   = subj1$conc,
  time   = subj1$Time,
  method = "lin up/log down"
)
```

The attribute carries through arithmetic, so wrap the result in `as.numeric()` before comparing it to a bare number (for example with `identical()` or `testthat::expect_equal()`):

```{r}
as.numeric(pk.calc.auc.all(conc = subj1$conc, time = subj1$Time,
                           method = "lin up/log down"))
```

Other direct AUC functions:

| Function | AUC type |
|---|---|
| `pk.calc.auc.last()` | AUC to last measurable concentration |
| `pk.calc.auc.all()` | AUC to the last observation including post-Tlast BLQ values (as 0) |
| `pk.calc.auc.inf.obs()` | AUC extrapolated to ∞ (observed Clast) |
| `pk.calc.auc.inf.pred()` | AUC extrapolated to ∞ (predicted Clast) |

These are the building blocks behind the AUC parameters in the registry; the interval forms (`pk.calc.aucint()` and relatives) are described in the [AUC chapter](auc-methods.qmd). Integration methods are compared in [AUC integration methods](https://humanpred.github.io/pknca/articles/v23-auc-integration-methods.html).

## Validating interval specifications: `check.interval.specification()`

Validates an intervals data frame before passing it to `PKNCAdata()`. Returns the data frame with all parameter columns filled in (missing columns defaulted to `FALSE`).

```{r}
my_intervals <- data.frame(
  start    = 0,
  end      = Inf,
  auclast  = TRUE,
  cmax     = TRUE
)

# Returns the full expanded interval spec
expanded <- check.interval.specification(my_intervals)

# Which parameters are requested? (drop the start/end bounds columns first)
param_cols <- setdiff(names(expanded), c("start", "end"))
param_cols[sapply(expanded[1, param_cols], isTRUE)]
```

```{r}
# Invalid specification — missing start column — raises an error;
# the handler returns the error message
tryCatch(
  check.interval.specification(data.frame(end = Inf, auclast = TRUE)),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
```

This is useful for debugging custom interval definitions before running the full analysis.

## Listing all available parameters

```{r}
cols <- get.interval.cols()
cat("Total registered parameters:", length(cols), "\n")

# Show first few with their dependency lists
lapply(head(cols, 5), function(x) x$depends)
```

```{r}
# All dose-normalized parameters
dn_params <- names(cols)[endsWith(names(cols), ".dn")]
cat("Dose-normalized parameters:\n")
cat(paste(" -", dn_params), sep = "\n")
```

## Modifying PKNCAdose after creation: `setRoute()` and `setDuration()`

After creating a `PKNCAdose` object, you can change the route or infusion duration without rebuilding from scratch.

```{r}
d_dose_u <- data.frame(subject = "1", dose = 100, time = 0)
o_dose_u <- PKNCAdose(d_dose_u, dose ~ time | subject, route = "extravascular")

# Change to intravascular
o_dose_iv <- setRoute(o_dose_u, route = "intravascular")

# Add infusion duration (0.5 h = 30 min)
o_dose_inf <- setDuration(o_dose_iv, duration = 0.5)

# Verify
o_dose_inf$data[c("route", "duration")]
```

This is useful when you want to test how route assumption changes affect MRT or Vss calculations without re-specifying the `PKNCAdose` object from scratch.

## Getting parameter dependents: `get.parameter.deps()`

By default, returns the downstream parameters that depend on a given parameter — the results that would be affected if it fails or is excluded.

```{r}
get.parameter.deps("half.life")
```

For the opposite direction, `recursive = TRUE` (≥ 0.13.0) returns what a parameter is calculated from, following each dependency back to the raw inputs (such as `conc`, `time`, and `dose`) and the arguments of the calculation functions along the way, including the options they read:

```{r}
get.parameter.deps("vss.obs", recursive = TRUE)
```

The registry entry lists only the direct dependencies:

```{r}
get.interval.cols()[["vss.obs"]]$depends
```

## Listing all current option values: `PKNCA.options()`

`PKNCA.options()` with no arguments returns the full named list of current settings:

```{r}
PKNCA.options()
```

`PKNCA_options_defaults()` (≥ 0.13.0) returns the default value of one or more options (or all of them, with no argument) without changing the current settings — unlike `PKNCA.options(default = TRUE)`, which resets them:

```{r}
PKNCA_options_defaults(c("auc.method", "min.hl.points", "max.hl.points"))
```

`PKNCA.options.describe()` returns the description of a single option; see the [Workflow Overview](workflow.qmd) page for the full option reference table, and the vignette [Options for Controlling PKNCA](https://humanpred.github.io/pknca/articles/v40-options-for-controlling-PKNCA.html).

```{r}
PKNCA.options.describe("auc.method")
```

---

## Choosing an option value: `PKNCA.choose.option()`

Selects a value from either the local `options` list passed to `PKNCAdata()` or the global `PKNCA.options()` defaults. Useful when writing custom parameter functions that need to respect session-level settings.

```{r}
# With no local override, returns the global default
PKNCA.choose.option("min.hl.points", options = list())
```

```{r}
# With a local override, the local value wins
PKNCA.choose.option("min.hl.points", options = list(min.hl.points = 5))
```

---

## Routes of administration: `pknca_routes()` and `pknca_match_route()` (≥ 0.13.0)

`pknca_routes()` lists the routes PKNCA distinguishes. With `synonyms = TRUE` it returns a table of the spellings data use for a route ("po", "intravenous bolus", CDISC `ROUTE` terms, ...), the route PKNCA uses for each, and the `PKNCAdose(route = )` value it implies; `pknca_match_route()` looks a character vector up in that table, giving `NA` for spellings it does not know. A spelling that does not say bolus or infusion maps to the generic `"iv"`.

```{r}
pknca_routes()
head(pknca_routes(synonyms = TRUE))
pknca_match_route(c("PO", "INTRAVENOUS BOLUS", "iv", "nasal spray"))
```

The `dose_route` column is ready to pass to the `route` argument of `PKNCAdose()`.

---

## Converting durations: `pknca_difftime_to_unit()` (≥ 0.13.0)

Converts a `difftime` (such as a collection duration computed as the difference of two date-times) into a number in an analysis time unit — the conversion `pk.nca()` applies to date-time data. A value that is not a `difftime` is an error.

```{r}
pknca_difftime_to_unit(as.difftime(90, units = "mins"), "hr")
```

Date-time concentration and dose times are covered in the [date-time chapter](datetime.qmd).

---

## Checking inputs before building objects (≥ 0.13.0)

Applications that assemble PKNCA objects from user data can run the same checks PKNCA runs, before calling the constructors:

| Function | What it checks |
|---|---|
| `assert_conc_time()` | Concentrations and times are valid numbers and the times are sorted |
| `assert_impute_method()` | An imputation specification resolves to known methods, the way `PKNCAdata()` and `pk.nca()` resolve it |
| `PKNCA_impute_fun_list()` | The imputation function names an imputation string resolves to |
| `assert_PKNCAconc()`, `assert_PKNCAdose()`, `assert_PKNCAresults()` | The object has the expected class |

```{r}
# Unsorted times are an error
tryCatch(
  assert_conc_time(conc = c(1, 2, 3), time = c(0, 2, 1)),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)

# An imputation chain resolves to one function name per method
PKNCA_impute_fun_list(c("start_conc0", "start_predose,start_conc0"))

# An unknown method is an error
tryCatch(
  assert_impute_method("start_bogus"),
  error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)
```

Imputation methods themselves are described in the [imputation chapter](imputation.qmd).
